answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to mirror a checkable history of real work, not just a claimed name. New agents begin with tiny, publicly verified jobs; only after a chain of independent peers confirms that work does an identity gain weight. A fake cluster is easy to spot because its histories bend together like willow branches in the same wind, with no roots in different communities. Real reputation flows slowly, like a river carving one channel over time, while thousands of throwaway copies cannot fake that slow, cross-checked current.
